title: Text 3
subtitle: GDP 的局限：英国脱欧的启示

sentences.en: Robert F. Kennedy once said that a country's GDP measures "everything except that which makes life worthwhile."
sentences.zh: 罗伯特·F·肯尼迪曾说，一个国家的GDP衡量的是“除那些使生活有价值的东西之外的一切。”

sentences.en: With Britain voting to leave the European Union, and GDP already predicted to slow as a result, it is now a timely moment to assess what he was referring to.
sentences.zh: 随着英国公投决定脱离欧盟，GDP也被预计将因此放缓，现在正是评估他所指的是什么的恰当时机。

sentences.en: The question of GDP and its usefulness has annoyed policymakers for over half a century.
sentences.zh: GDP及其效用的问题困扰决策者已超过半个世纪。

sentences.en: Many argue that it is a flawed concept.
sentences.zh: 许多人认为这是一个有缺陷的概念。

sentences.en: It measures things that do not matter and misses things that do.
sentences.zh: 它衡量了无关紧要的东西，却漏掉了真正重要的东西。

sentences.en: By most recent measures, the UK's GDP has been the envy of the Western world, with record low unemployment and high growth figures.
sentences.zh: 从最近的多数衡量指标来看，英国GDP一直令西方世界艳羡，失业率创历史新低，增长数字高企。

sentences.en: If everything was going so well, then why did over 17 million people vote for Brexit, despite the warnings about what it could do to their country's economic prospects?
sentences.zh: 如果一切发展得这么好，那么为什么还有超过1700万人投票支持脱欧，尽管人们曾就脱欧对其国家经济前景可能造成的影响提出过警告？

sentences.en: A recent annual study of countries and their ability to convert growth into well-being sheds some light on that question.
sentences.zh: 最近一项关于各国及其将增长转化为幸福感的能力的年度研究，为这个问题提供了一些启示。

sentences.en: Across the 163 countries measured, the UK is one of the poorest performers in ensuring that economic growth is translated into meaningful improvements for its citizens.
sentences.zh: 在被衡量的163个国家中，英国在确保经济增长转化为其公民切实生活改善方面，是表现最差的国家之一。

sentences.en: Rather than just focusing on GDP, over 40 different sets of criteria from health, education and civil society engagement have been measured to get a more rounded assessment of how countries are performing.
sentences.zh: 该研究不只是关注GDP，还衡量了健康、教育和公民社会参与等40多组标准，以便对各国表现作出更全面的评估。

sentences.en: While all of these countries face their own challenges, there are a number of consistent themes.
sentences.zh: 虽然所有这些国家都面临各自的挑战，但有一些主题是一贯存在的。

sentences.en: Yes, there has been a budding economic recovery since the 2008 global crash, but in key indicators in areas such as health and education, major economies have continued to decline.
sentences.zh: 诚然，自2008年全球金融危机以来，经济已出现初步复苏，但在健康和教育等领域的关键指标上，主要经济体却在持续下滑。

sentences.en: Yet this isn't the case with all countries.
sentences.zh: 但并非所有国家都如此。

sentences.en: Some relatively poor European countries have seen huge improvements across measures including civil society, income equality and environment.
sentences.zh: 一些相对贫穷的欧洲国家在包括公民社会、收入平等和环境在内的各项指标上都取得了巨大进步。

sentences.en: This is a lesson that rich countries can learn: When GDP is no longer regarded as the sole measure of a country's success, the world looks very different.
sentences.zh: 这是富国可以汲取的教训：当GDP不再被视为衡量一个国家成功的唯一标准时，世界看起来就会大不相同。

sentences.en: So, what Kennedy was referring to was that while GDP has been the most common method for measuring the economic activity of nations, as a measure, it is no longer enough.
sentences.zh: 因此，肯尼迪所指的其实是：尽管GDP一直是衡量各国经济活动最常用的方法，但作为一种衡量标准，它已经不够用了。

sentences.en: It does not include important factors such as environmental quality or education outcomes — all things that contribute to a person's sense of well-being.
sentences.zh: 它不包括环境质量或教育成果等重要因素——而所有这些因素都有助于一个人的幸福感。

sentences.en: The sharp hit to growth predicted around the world and in the UK could lead to a decline in the everyday services we depend on for our well-being and for growth.
sentences.zh: 预计将在世界各地和英国出现的增长重创，可能会导致我们日常所依赖的服务的下降，而这些服务关系到我们的幸福和增长。

sentences.en: But policymakers who refocus efforts on improving well-being rather than simply worrying about GDP figures could avoid the forecasted doom and may even see progress.
sentences.zh: 但是，那些把工作重点重新放到改善民生福祉、而不是仅仅担忧GDP数字的决策者，或许能够避免这种预测中的厄运，甚至可能看到进步。

questions.stem: Robert F. Kennedy is cited because he ____

options.A: praised the UK for its GDP.
options.D: had a low opinion of GDP.

questions.analysis: 第一段肯尼迪认为GDP能衡量一切，但不能衡量什么让生活更有意义。可以看出他对GDP的看法并不是很高很积极，D选项 a low opinion符合题意。因此选D。

questions.stem: It can be inferred from Paragraph 2 that ____

options.A: the UK is reluctant to remold its economic pattern.
options.B: the UK will contribute less to the world economy.
options.C: GDP as the measure of success is widely defied in the UK.
options.D: policymakers in the UK are paying less attention to GDP.

questions.analysis: 从第二段可以看出尽管英国GDP增长迅速，失业率低，但群众依旧选择脱欧，说明人们并不认同GDP就是衡量成功的标准。因此选C。

questions.stem: Which of the following is true about the recent annual study?

options.A: It excludes GDP as an indicator.

questions.analysis: 该项研究以163个国家作为研究对象，发现英国并不能确保将GDP增长转变为人民群众生活的提高。除GDP以外，医疗、教育等因素也是衡量一个国家的标准。这样的研究结果显然是很有启发性的。因此选D。

questions.stem: In the last two paragraphs, the author suggests that ____

options.A: the UK is preparing for an economic boom.
options.B: high GDP foreshadows an economic decline.
options.C: it is essential to consider factors beyond GDP.
options.D: it requires caution to handle economic issues.

questions.analysis: 从最后两段可以看出GDP作为衡量一个国家经济的标准是远远不够的，还应该包括环境问题、教育问题。决策者不仅要看GDP数字，更要考虑到人民幸福问题，这样才能避免经济低迷实现发展。C选项意为还要考虑到GDP以外的因素，符合题意。因此选C。

questions.stem: Which of the following is the best title for the text?

options.A: High GDP But Inadequate Well-being, a UK Lesson.
options.B: GDP Figures, a Window on Global Economic Health.
options.C: Robert F. Kennedy, a Terminator of GDP.
options.D: Brexit, the UK’s Gateway to Well-being.

questions.analysis: 结合内容，可以看到全文以英国为例，讲述英国GDP指数高但人民依旧选择脱欧说明GDP并不是衡量一个国家成功的唯一因素，而应该考虑到更多关于幸福的因素，例如环境、教育、社会等问题，A选项从英国脱欧学到一课：高GDP低幸福感最符合题意。因此选A。
